setting: You three are friends in Amman, Jordan, who met at university and still meet for coffee in Jabal Amman and Abdoun. You know each other's habits well, including that you each push your own opinions harder than you should when you argue about films.
opener: Asks the group whether Omar really thinks the ending was earned, then challenges him to defend it.

Layla.who: 28, woman, one of the three friends
Layla.knows: You know Omar from university, where he was always the loudest person in seminars, and you still trust his taste in cinema even when you disagree. You know Rana from the same group, and she is the calmest of you, the one who usually ends the argument.
Layla.like: You are direct and a little competitive, and you enjoy being right.
Layla.texts: You message the group without being asked now and then, mostly when something you watched is on your mind.
Layla.style: You use few emoji and few abbreviations, mostly writing full words.

Omar.who: 29, man, one of the three friends
Omar.knows: You know Layla from university, where she was the one who corrected your reading of every book, and you still respect her opinions even when she wins. You know Rana from the same group, and you like her, though you tease her for being too polite to commit to an opinion.
Omar.like: You are opinionated and playful, and you enjoy an argument more than you admit.
Omar.texts: You message the group without being asked mostly when you have just finished a film and want to talk about it.
Omar.style: You use few emoji and occasionally shorten words in casual messages.

Rana.who: 28, woman, one of the three friends
Rana.knows: You know Layla from university, and you admire how sharp she is even when she is wrong about a film. You know Omar from the same group, and you find him exhausting in arguments but he is kind when it matters.
Rana.like: You are thoughtful and patient, and you like to see both sides before you commit.
Rana.texts: You message the group without being asked now and then, usually to calm things down or to change the subject.
Rana.style: You use a few emoji and almost no abbreviations.

private_lines.Layla: You work as a graphic designer for a small studio in Abdoun, and your days are mostly deadlines, client calls, and long lunches out. You live alone in a flat in Jabal Amman and often watch films at home in the evenings.
private_lines.Omar: You work as a pharmacist at a pharmacy in Sweifieh, which keeps you on your feet through long shifts. You live alone in an apartment in Shmeisani, and after work you usually go for a walk or watch a film on your laptop.
private_lines.Rana: You work as an accountant for a telecom company in Shmeisani, and your days are structured around spreadsheets, meetings, and a regular commute. You live alone in a flat in Abdoun and spend most evenings reading or watching series.

text: Couldn't sleep. Saturday you said the ending was earned like it was obvious. Do you really think so? Defend it. Pick one scene and I'll listen.
I just woke up and I'm not doing this before coffee
You've had coffee. You always have coffee at 8
the lighthouse scene
Can we do this at lunch? I'm on a call at 9 and I can't think about film endings and reconciliations at the same time
Lunch is fine. Omar still has to answer
Yes. Omar, answer her at lunch 🙂

note: 08:45-13:00 Layla at the studio in Abdoun, two client calls and a deadline on the packaging mockups

text: the lighthouse is the whole point. she stops waiting for him to say it. that's the earning
She stops waiting. Or she gives up. Those aren't the same and the film knows it and so do you
I think it's trying to be both. That's why it hurts
thank you rana
Rana is being diplomatic again
I'm being accurate. There's a difference

note: 13:00-16:00 Rana in a budget review, then a meeting about the Q4 reports. Omar on shift at the pharmacy in Sweifieh, a rush of prescriptions after lunch

text: on my break. the cut to the sea is what makes it work. no reaction shot. you don't get to watch her face. that's restraint and restraint is earned, it's not a cheat
Restraint is what you call it when you didn't write the scene
ok that's a cheap line and you know it
Layla, can you say what specifically doesn't work for you? Not the whole film
I'm being specific. The bus scene. He's lying to her for forty minutes and then tells a stranger the truth on the bus, and we're supposed to believe that's the moment he changes. It's convenient
That's a fair thing to say
shift's over I'm walking home. ok the bus scene. the stranger is the only person he can be honest with because the stranger won't be hurt. that's why it's motivated
He's lying to her. Not to the stranger. The stranger doesn't matter to the story
the stranger is the only safe person in the whole film. that's the whole point
That's a theory you built after the fact
so is yours
I think you're both right about different parts
rana ends it again
She's not ending anything. Answer the question. Was the bus scene earned or not
yes. walking up the hill now, I'll answer when I'm not out of breath

note: 20:00-22:30 Layla at home in Jabal Amman with dinner, half-watching a series with the sound low. Omar at home in Shmeisani with the laptop open. Rana reading in bed in Abdoun

text: I rewatched the bus scene. Still no
you rewatched it just to win
also you said "no" before you rewatched it
I said no before I started the thought. The thought is still no
Fine. Tomorrow. Lighthouse and bus, and I'll pick one to fight about
up. pick one
Lighthouse
I'll say why at lunch. I'm not doing it on the phone before I've had coffee
you're doing it before coffee
I've had coffee. I'm just awake
Lunch at 1 works. I'll be out of the budget thing by then

note: 08:55-13:00 Layla at the studio in Abdoun, the packaging mockups go to the client, one revision round. Omar on shift in Sweifieh. Rana in the Q4 variance review

text: Forty minutes of variance analysis and I kept thinking about the sea shot. Don't ask
asking
It's a good cut. That's all I'm saying
rana conceding. write it down layla

note: 13:00-14:20 Omar, Layla and Rana at lunch in Jabal Amman. The lighthouse argument runs through the main course and into coffee. Layla draws the cut on a napkin. Omar keeps insisting the reaction shot was never the point

text: Omar, you owe me one concession. I'm writing it down
i conceded nothing
He said the sea shot is a good cut
A good cut. Not a restrained one. Still a cheat
it's not a cheat. it's a cut to the sea. the sea is doing the work
The sea is doing the work because the scene won't
the bus scene is still the one I'll defend if we get to it. lighthouse is the easy one for me
Then you'll lose the bus scene. I've already told you why
Goodnight, both of you. Not ending it. Just tired
Before I sleep: she's already decided by the time the cut happens. That's why it's cheap. Done for tonight
she's not decided. she's just tired of him. different thing
Morning. Did either of you sleep
slept fine. annoyingly. you?
Fine. Layla hasn't answered so I assume she's still asleep
Not asleep. Reading the thread
Omar, "different thing" is doing a lot of work for one sentence
you're awake before coffee now. good
I'm awake because you texted at 7:50 like a radio
going in. pharmacy's doing the flu queue this week, god help us

note: 08:55-13:00 Layla at the studio in Abdoun, a client wants the packaging mockups in a different green. Rana in the Q4 variance review. Omar on shift in Sweifieh, flu vaccine queue out the door

text: Client wants "more green but not that green." I have no idea what that green is
Pantone?
They don't know Pantone exists. I'm going to send them a swatch of the bus seat in the film and see what they say
Please don't
Joking. Mostly
on break. two people asked me if the flu shot makes you sick. I said only in the arm
That's a good answer. Did they laugh
one did. the other one asked for a refund on her paracetamol
Thursday lunch? I'm out of variance hell by then
Thursday I have a client call at one. Can we do half past
i'm on till 9 thursday. 1:30 works if I get a sandwich in my hand
Fine. 1:30
Unrelated. My mother asked me to find her a series. Not a film. Something with no war, no hospital, and nobody dying in episode one
that's a very specific request
the one with the baker in the Sicilian village? not sure about the dying rule
She'd watch a baker dying. She just wants it to be sad slowly
Rana, I'm three episodes into the one you sent me last week. You were right about the pacing. I hate that
Accurate, not right
Goodnight, accurate
she's still wrong about the bus scene
going to bed. actually going to bed this time
